Webster-UESTC 20th Anniversary Celebration Held in Chengdu

December 18, 2023

With an audience of more than 300 attendees, the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China (UESTC) and Webster University celebrated 20 years of continuous MBA education in Chengdu, China on Dec. 10. Ryan Guffey, director general for global campuses, served as a keynote speaker alongside Zeng Yong, the president of UESTC. Webster University President Julian Schuster attended remotely and commended the alumni, students and professors on creating an innovative environment that brings the best of both American and Chinese entrepreneurialism together.

Director General for Global Campuses Ryan Guffey speaks at the event.

President Yong, who, in his previous role as Dean of the School of Management and

Economics, helped establish the partnership 20 years ago, spoke at the event.

"UESTC is one of the leading universities in China, especially endowed in STEM teaching

and research, and, thanks to Webster, also in the areas of business and management."

Webster University provides the MBA in Chengdu as a joint partnership between the

School of Management and Economics at UESTC and the Walker School of Business and

Technology at Webster University, tailored with an international focus and for already

or soon to be executives.

Dr. Liu Bo, the UESTC Co-Director of the Joint Program, asked the audience, comprised

of alumni and current students, to envision the next 20 years. He encouraged them

to traverse onwards in their careers while supporting their classmates and fellow

alumni as they continue to create opportunity for all who are part of the partnership.

Ontario Tech University celebrates 20 years

Year-long 20th anniversary will celebrate and highlight two decades of milestones and accomplishments

September 4, 2023

Since first opening its doors on September 4, 2003, Ontario Tech University has grown into a highly sought-after post-secondary education institution for learning, teaching and working. With more than 11,000 students, 29,000 alumni and 2,500 employees, the university has an amazing story to tell—one that spans two decades of incredible milestones and accomplishments.

The university will kick off its year-long 20th anniversary with a BBQ for the campus community on Thursday, September 7. Throughout the year, numerous events and initiatives will showcase the university's past, present and future, as we celebrate with students, faculty, staff, alumni, partners, donors, the community and beyond.

From humble beginnings to a thriving university

On opening day in 2003, Ontario Tech enrolled an inaugural class of 947 students. Over the years, the university has evolved and experienced rapid growth in enrolment, academic and recreational programming, student support, infrastructure, donations, partnerships and research grants. Throughout it all the university has stayed true to its ethos: understanding and using technology for the betterment of society.

"Ontario Tech declared itself the province's first 'laptop-based' university when it opened, but as we all know, technology changes rapidly and relentlessly, and it remains at the heart of all that we do," says Dr. Steven Murphy, President and Vice-Chancellor.

Opening Ceremony of the Tirana Campus - Academic Year 2024/2025

"The College of Europe is much more than an ordinary university. When our continent still laid in ruins after World War 2, a group of European pioneers came up with a visionary idea: let's build an academy to raise the leaders of tomorrow that will unite Europe. A new generation for a new beginning. That was one of the first building blocks of European Integration. Before coal and steel, it all started with the College." said the president of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, during her keynote speech.

The Opening Ceremony of the academic year 2024-2025 of the College of Europe – Tirana Campus took place on Wednesday, October 23, 2023, in the Pyramid of Tirana.

Prime Minister Edi Rama addressed our students and underlined how historic this moment is! The rector, Federica Mogherini, declared the first academic year on the Tirana campus officially open.

Our student representatives shared moving personal stories about their journey to the College.

Alumni Anniversaries: Reflecting on 10 Years of Excellence and Inspirational Journeys

On October 10, 2023, I celebrated the 10th anniversary of receiving the NSW International Student of the Year Award (Higher Education) at the iconic Sydney Opera House. As I took a moment between my parenting duties to my newborn to reflect on my journey, I felt compelled to pay tribute to the many colleagues and friends who have been an integral part of my life. In particular, I want to honour two outstanding individuals, Khin Yew Chong and Wan Hoe G. by sharing their stories.

Khin Yew the engineer

I first crossed paths with Khin Yew, an alumnus of UNSW, in 2011 at a new student meet-and-greet event. Both of us were actively involved in student organisations. He served as the Chair of the Malaysian Students' Council of Australia NSW (MASCA NSW) , while I held the position of National President of the Council of International Students Australia Inc. (CISA). Among our notable achievements was the initiation of the "My Study, My Career" International Student Forum at the iconic Lower Town Hall in Sydney on March 27, 2013. This student-led initiative, in collaboration with the City of Sydney, the Ethnic Communities' Council of NSW, and the Council of International Students Australia, aimed to connect international students with alumni, employers, and volunteering organisations.
